answer: Copying the same citations across 283 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 283 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the nebula index resolves every citation against the vine checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the echo audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 30 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
